q: What is the minimum distance required between roof eaves and rear/side property lines?
n: “Eaves, canopies, awnings (or media agua) over required windows shall not be less than 750 millimeters from the side and rear property lines.”

q: Firewalls are not allowed for R1 developments. However, an abutment of up to ___ in height is allowed, provided that above 1.50m, the abutment is made of perforated concrete blocks.
n: For R-1 (single-detached) zoning, true firewalls aren't permitted, but an abutment/fence-type wall up to 3.20m is, with the portion above 1.50m required to be perforated concrete blocks (to preserve light/ventilation to the yard).

q: For a sloping lot with a 4.00m difference between the highest and lowest points of the lot, where will the established grade line be for building height determination?
o: The lowest point of the lot
The highest point of the lot
The average between the two points
ref: IRR Rule VII — Building Height Limit (established grade line)
n: When the difference in elevation across the lot exceeds 3 meters, the established grade line for measuring building height is the average between the highest and lowest points; below that 3m threshold, the lower point governs instead.

q: What is the minimum parking slot size for an articulated truck?
ref: IRR Rule VII, Table VII.4 — Parking Slot Requirements
n: Table VII.4 sets 3.60m x 18.00m as the minimum bay size for an articulated truck, distinct from the smaller stalls prescribed for cars, jeepneys/vans, and standard trucks.

q: If you add the ISA and the USA, what will you get?
ref: IRR Rule VIII, Table VIII.1 — PSO / ISA / USA / TOSL
n: Total Open Space within Lot (TOSL) is made up of Impervious Surface Area (ISA) plus Unpaved Surface Area (USA): TOSL = ISA + USA.

q: If you subtract the ISA from the construction area, what will you get?
ref: IRR Rule VIII, Table VIII.1 — PSO / ISA / USA / TOSL
n: Maximum Allowable Construction Area (MACA/CA) is PSO + ISA, so rearranging gives CA − ISA = PSO (Percentage of Site Occupancy, expressed as footprint area).

q: What is the minimum area for habitable rooms, according to the National Building Code?
ref: PD 1096, §806 — Size and Dimensions of Rooms
n: Section 806 sets 6.00 square meters as the minimum floor area for rooms for human habitation (with 2.00m as the least horizontal dimension) — larger than the 3.00 sqm minimum for kitchens.

q: What is the minimum air space provision per person for habitable rooms?
n: Section 807 requires 14 cubic meters of air space per person for habitable/bedrooms, compared to 3.00 cu.m. for school rooms and 12.00 cu.m. for workshops, factories, and offices.

q: What is the minimum ceiling height required for the seventh floor of an artificially-ventilated building?
n: Section 805 sets the first storey at 2.70m and the second at 2.40m, with the “succeeding stories” — the 7th floor included — needing only an unobstructed clearance of not less than 2.10m.

q: For forest areas, the NBC requires at least _____ of easement for each side of the waterway.
ref: PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines), Art. 51
n: The public-use easement along waterway banks is 3m in urban areas, 20m in agricultural areas, and 40m in forest areas — a Water Code rule the Building Laws reviewer folds into site-easement questions.

q: Rowhouses 1-3 storeys high fall under which zoning classification?
ref: IRR Rule VII — Zoning Classification Tables
n: Rowhouses of 1 to 3 storeys are classified under R-3 (the basic multi-unit residential category), as opposed to R-2 (duplex/single-attached) or the non-residential GI and C-1 classifications.

q: What are the allowable firewall configurations for an R2 project?
o: Allowed on one side of property
Allowed on both sides of the property
Allowed on one side and the rear
n: R-2 (duplex/single-attached) projects are only allowed a firewall on one side of the property — reflecting that only one common wall is expected between adjoining units.

q: For R-4 projects, firewalls may be allowed on both sides of the property. What is the maximum height for these firewalls?
n: R-4 firewalls on both sides of the property are capped at 3 storeys, beyond which a firewall configuration is no longer allowed and a yard/setback must be used instead.

q: All of these affect the maximum total gross floor area given by Table 7.1 except for:
o: Use or non-use of firewalls for the project
ref: IRR Rule VII, Table VII.1 — Allowable Maximum TGFA
n: Table VII.1 keys the maximum TGFA to the zoning designation, lot type, and firewall use (which drive the allowable PSO), but road width is not a factor in the TGFA table itself — it affects other checks, like BHL from Table VIII.2/8.3, but not TGFA.

q: When the only road fronting a property is 5 meters wide and the property is zoned as R1, the maximum height allowed for the project is
ref: IRR Rule VII/VIII — Building Height Limit by Road Width & Zoning
n: For an R-1 lot fronting only a 5-meter road, the Building Height Limit tables cap the project at 2.5 storeys — narrow road frontage constrains height even where the zoning would otherwise allow more.
